subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: REFINEMENT to claim.law.inline-frame-candidates-need-a-target-minus-ours-delta-census.20260831.v1, which calls a POSITIVE target-minus-ours delta 'the productive direction' on the strength of one specimen (LoadPlyrData, +152, real 1635 -> 465). Measured across six functions this session, THE SIGN OF THE DELTA DOES NOT PREDICT WHETHER CLOSING IT PAYS, and closing a delta EXACTLY is routinely achievable while still losing on every retained metric. Both signs produced both outcomes: positive deltas gave one large win (StringTextHeightSub +32, fuzzy 72.19 -> 96.22) and one exact-closure-that-scored-worse (StringTextWidthSub +12, frame 232 -> 248 = target, slot count 7 -> 5 matching target, multiset 21t -> 18t, yet real 163 -> 168 and fuzzy 73.34 -> 71.91, reverted); negative deltas gave one clean win (sndFxQueAddEx -8, real 30 -> 12, kept) and one exact-closure-that-scored-worse (AudioWithName -16, frame 72 -> 56 with BOTH referenced slots equal to target, yet real 44 -> 62 and fuzzy 95.94 -> 95.75, reverted). WHAT ACTUALLY PREDICTS THE PAYOFF is whether the frame was the LAST structural defect or merely the FIRST one you happened to measure. The frame constant is a slot-alignment fact; it does not carry code. Where the instruction stream was already essentially right, closing the frame converted the function (StringTextHeightSub finished with the whole entry region byte-identical; sndFxQueAddEx finished at multiset 0t whenever both typed bases were declared). Where the frame was masking an independent schedule defect, closing it merely re-permuted the surviving disagreement and the score got worse - AudioWithName's closure re-ordered a 7-instruction prologue into 9-target/8-ours unpaired words on top of a three-cycle register rotation, and three distinct source axes then produced byte-identical output. OPERATIONAL RULE, in this order. (1) Measure the delta with the alias-aware recipe and CALIBRATE against the five published values first; an uncalibrated census is measuring something else. (2) Read the opcode MULTISET before deciding to spend the session: a function already at multiset 0t-1t with a frame delta (sndFxQueAddEx 0t, StartExplosion 1t) is the profitable shape, because the frame is demonstrably the only thing left; a function whose multiset differs by 9t-21t has independent structural work and the frame is not the headline. (3) Close the frame, then RE-MEASURE BOTH real and fuzzy before keeping - an exact frame is not self-justifying evidence, and this session reverted two byte-exact frame closures on that basis. (4) Because a frame probe reads NEUTRAL or misleading on real (confirmed again on all four functions), never let 'real did not move' stand in for 'the frame did not move' - grep the stwu constant. COROLLARY ON THE INLINE MECHANISM: claim.law.inlined-callee-frames-reserve-dead-frame-bottom's quantitative rule predicts the caller reserves the inlinee's own frame per expansion site, and that held EXACTLY twice (AudioFloatNotZero, 4 sites x 4 bytes = the 16-byte surplus, removed by de-inlining; TextLinesWidth, 2 sites x 16 bytes = +32, added by introducing the helper) - but it FAILS when the inlinee's locals all registerize: a u8[16] array declared inside a static inline helper reserved NOTHING, because MWCC eliminated the unused array outright. So the reservation is a property of the ORIGINAL source's helper, not a lever you can pull from inside a helper you wrote; when you need to ADD a dead low region and the helper will not produce it, a pad declared LAST at function scope does land below every other local and shifts the whole slot set up by exactly its size (measured, StringTextHeightSub, 32 bytes, all seven slots).
